One slow step, and the chief drew closer. Not a trace of last time's arrogant leisure remained.

Only composure backed by real skill.
Yes. Strong, this woman.

With that fresh confirmation, my idea of using the back of the blade was dismissed. Like that I could not possibly win.

A sword is made to strike the enemy with its edge. Not only a question of sharpness. Shape, balance, hilt wrapping, even the position of the grip ornaments: all of it assumes the edge will be used.

Ignore all that, and the sword's performance suffers. She was already better than me. Give myself an additional disadvantage also, and my small chance would leave before I could catch it.

Use the sword properly, then. Avoid the vital points. Or stop the stroke just short.

...Which sounded hardly easier than winning with the back of the blade. Still, even a paper's thickness nearer to victory was a choice I had a duty to make.

Not only my own life was resting on this back.

Slowly, slowly, she slid her feet along the ground and closed in. A tortoise's progress. That was precisely the frightening part.

Stand still, and I gave up the initiative in controlling the distance. But measuring it became easier for me. However slowly, she was moving; I was not. That advantage, at least, was certain.

Best to find my chance there.

　首領はじわり、じわりと、地面を足裏で摺って間合
を詰めてきていた。

　姿勢を、重心を、崩さぬままに遅く遅くゆっくりと
ひた歩むのはまさに至難の業だ。
　姿勢の維持は早足の方が遥かに易く済む。

　自転車を例に引き出せば自明の事。
　歩くよりも遅い速度で自転車を乗りこなすなど、誰
にできようか？

　首領の遅足は、その離れ業を――重心の完全制御を
意味している。
　本能的な怯えが、俺の背筋を冷たく這い登った。

　……つまりはこういう事だ。
　彼女はこの歩法により、間合が<ruby>斬り間<rt>・・・</rt></ruby>に達する瞬間
を、ずれなく無駄なく完全に掌握し、最高の機に一刀
を繰り出す事ができる。

　これと拮抗するには、同じ戦機をこちらも掴むしか
ない。
　俺は緊張に強張りかける眼球を辛うじて宥め、適度
に弛緩させて視野を安定させた。

　足は、その場に留める。
　これも一つの選択であった。

　敵の歩法に対してこちらも歩法にて応じ、敵の間合
掌握を乱し己のみ間合を奪おうと図る――それも一途。
　だが放棄した。そこに勝負を挑んではおそらく勝て
ない。

　間合の取り合いとなれば、何よりも実戦経験が物を
言う。
　高々数年ばかりの兵役と幾度かの仕合の経験のみで、
六波羅武者の歴戦ぶりに敵し得るとは些かも思えない。

　静止して待てば、間の取り合いについてはアドバン
テージを譲ることになるものの、距離の把握において
はこちらの方が容易であり優位となる。微速ながらも
敵は動いている以上、この点は揺るがない。

　そこに勝機を見出すに如かず。

In the morning mist, no trace of her breath showed. Her breathing was completely hidden. Mine also—was I hiding it that well? Or was I only hoping?

Let the enemy read your breath and you might as well write your whole schedule on a blackboard. Here, madam. At this moment I cannot respond; kindly attack then.

Muscles move the body. Their power depends on breathing. Ordinarily, exhaling gives more force than holding the breath, and holding gives more than inhaling.

So she must not detect me drawing air into my lungs, the moment when every muscle's power drops. For that, my outgoing breath had to be as gentle as possible.

Hide the exhale, hide the inhale also.
Quiet use of the lungs was essential...

Meanwhile the distance had narrowed.

As if shaved away with a small knife, it was approaching one particular measure.

One particular measure.

The distance for cutting.

ない。
　それには、吐息の勢いを可能な限り緩めることだ。

That was why I had let the chance pass. Perhaps she knew the Dropping Cut, or another counter that let me begin first and lose afterward. Such a possibility, I could not wave away with 'kuch nahin hoga.' Something very final might happen.

...Possibly my only chance had already gone. Doubt crawled around my heart. I shook it off and measured the distance again.

My favorable strip was nearly finished. One more breath and we could both strike.

Three choices. Start now, while my reach was longer. Start when we could both reach. Or wait there for her to start.

Naturally, she also had choices. Opponent hai, furniture nahin. She was not obliged to remain whatever my calculation required.

First: attack now. If she answered with the Dropping Cut or a similar counter, I lost. Otherwise my head start in the sword race gave me the win.

Second: attack within mutual range. If she attacked too, we were even; sword speed would decide. If she waited to counter, I lost.

Third: wait for her. If she came, I won—provided I could actually perform the Striking Tide. That small matter of ability still applied. If she did not come, nothing changed.

Har taraf kuch na kuch. Every choice had its own difficulty. Which danger frightened me most? That would decide it.

Her sword speed? Then start now. Once we both entered range, even an equal contest was the best I could hope for.

Her counter? Then the first two choices were finished. Third only. Wait.

Which?
...The decision was already made.

だから見送った。
　首領が切落ないしはそれと同質の術、相手に先制を
許しながら後より勝つ迎撃技法を心得ている危険性に
ついて、考慮に値せずとは思い切りかねた。

　…………もしかすると、俺は唯一の勝機を逃したの
かもしれない。
　心臓の周辺に<ruby>ざわざわ<rt>・・・・</rt></ruby>と蠢く迷いを振り捨て、気を
新たに間合を測り直す。

　俺の優越距離は終わりかけていた。
　あと一呼吸後……双方の<ruby>打ち間<rt>レンジ</rt></ruby>となる。

　現在この時点で、俺には三つの選択肢があった。
　優越距離で仕掛けるのが一。相互攻撃の距離で仕掛
けるのが一。相互攻撃の距離で敵が仕掛けて来るのを
待つのが一。

　これに対応する形で、相手の側にも選択肢があると
いうことになる。

　まず第一の選択。
　こちらの優越距離で仕掛けた場合――相手が切落の
ような技をもって応じるなら、こちらの敗となる。
　そうでなければ剣速の差で勝。

　第二の選択。
　相撃の距離で仕掛け――相手も同様に仕掛けて来た
なら優劣は無し。剣速で勝敗は決する。
　敵が切落を期して待ち構えたなら敗。

　第三の選択。
　敵の仕掛けを待ち――望み通りに敵が来たならば勝。
〝打潮〟の剣理を俺の技量で全うできるなら、だが。
　敵が来なかったなら、状勢は動かず。

　いずれの方途も一長一短。
　選択の決め手は、敵の何を最も恐れるかという判断
だった。

　運剣の速度を最も恐れるとするなら、先にスタート
を切れる今こそ仕掛けねばならない。
　相互攻撃の間合に入った後では、互角以下の勝負に
しかならないのだ。

　そうではなく、迎撃技を最大の脅威と設定するなら、
第一・第二の選択は無いということになる。
　選ぶべきは第三。待ちの姿勢だ。

　どちらか。
　……だが、この決断は既に下している。

en.html:
No. I rejected the suggestion. Peechhe hato, and helplessness came along immediately.

Moving backward, I would lose the forward drive needed to strike. No counter to fear, weight going the wrong way, defence unable to hold properly. She could cut through me without difficulty.

Perhaps she would overlook it? Arre, how generous my mind had become toward my survival. Retreat was one of my options. She could hardly have forgotten it merely because remembering would inconvenience me.

Move back, and she would come. At once.

...No escape.
Time khareedna bhi nahin. I could not even buy time.

It kept leaving free of charge. Each bit gone brought me nearer the distance where the sword in my two hands would become useless.

...But killing her had never been my intention. Less killing power, surely that was desirable?

Bas. Such a helpful thought. My sword would politely adjust itself between 'unable to stop her' and 'kills her,' choosing exactly the force I wanted? Perhaps afterward it would apologise for the inconvenience also.

Enough power meant enough to cut bone.
Below that, bone would not be cut.

She came close. We exchanged strokes. My sword arrived first, even. It might wound her shoulder a few centimetres deep.

Then what?

She would not stop. A hundredth of an instant later, her blade would reach me. Fatal wound.

Haar gaya. I lost.

Then not an exchange. What if I alone landed a blow? Even if it did not settle the match, could I weaken her and turn matters my way?

Striking Tide. The Dropping Cut principle. Suppress her blade first, then cut. Or evade the stroke with my body, and then...

しかし、俺は自分の発想を一蹴した。
　後退すればその刹那、俺は<ruby>死に体<rt>・・・</rt></ruby>となる。

　前進して敵に打ち込んでゆく勢力を失う。
　それこそ、彼女にすれば勝機だ。迎撃の恐れはなく、
また体重が後ろへ流れているとなれば防御も踏ん張り
が利かない。斬り崩すのは造作ない。

　彼女がその勝機を掴み損ねると信じるのは如何にも
甘かろう。
　対手、つまり俺の取り得る手立ての一つとして後退
を考慮に入れていないとは考えられない。

　退けば必ず食い付いてくる。

　……逃げ場、無し。
　時間稼ぎの策すらも。

　時間はただ喪失に喪失を重ね、
　俺の死を意味する刻限へと近付いてゆく。

　両の腕に保持される太刀が意味を無くす、その距離
が接近する。

　……元より、この敵手を殺すつもりはないのだ。
　殺傷力を失う、それ自体は良しとしてもいい。

　だが打撃力の減衰が殺傷力以下<ruby>制圧力<rt>・・・</rt></ruby>以上にうまく
収まるかと云うと――
　虫の良い期待であろう。

　殺傷力が有るとは、骨まで断てるという事だ。
　それが無いとは、骨は断てないという事だ。

　このまま間合が侵され、そして斬り合いになったと
して――しかも速度優り、先にこちらの刃が相手の体
に達したとして。
　俺の太刀は敵の肩口を数<ruby>糎<rt>センチ</rt></ruby>は抉るだろう。

　しかし敵は止まるまい。
　一瞬の百分の一程の時間の後、敵の刃が達し、俺は
骨から内臓まで存分に斬り裂かれて果てる。

　敗北だ。

　ならば、相打ちではなく――
　一方的に、一撃を加えられるなら？　その一撃では
勝負を決められずとも、相手を弱らせ、流れを有利に
変えられるのではないか。

　打潮――切落の剣理で敵の剣を封じた上で斬れば。
　あるいは体捌きを駆使して一撃を躱せば……

Dying was not a matter of my convenience alone.

I struggled to hold on to the feeling in my limbs. Like a drowning man grabbing at straw, probably.

Every effort added another zero. Add as many as you liked, still nothing useful. The malicious surge carrying my mind and body away did not weaken even out of pity. It sneered and continued its work.

The feeling went first from below.
...My legs and hips were gone.

Where had they gone?
No, nonsense. Look down and they would be there.

But I could not give my eyes permission to go inspecting. The enemy was in FRONT...!

Desperately I kept my gaze ahead, though the smallest lapse threatened to send it downward. And while looking ahead, I could not disprove this ridiculous idea that my legs and hips did not exist.

Was I even standing?
I seemed to be floating.

Sword in hand, flying through the sky.
Just like an armoured warrior, then. The thought came as if in a dream.

An armoured warrior could actually lose both legs and not be greatly troubled. Up there, they were only parts for controlling posture.

Two legs were supposed to be supporting me. Find them.

Not the sky. I was not an armoured warrior.
Therefore the feet were definitely there.

Armoured swordsmanship did not rely on stepping in. But this was the ground. Forget the feet and I could not deliver a proper blow.

Without stepping in,
the power, the range—

My cutting range remained.
It had not been lost.

She must have understood that too. Otherwise, why had she not struck at once?

Balance. Bas, that much I had shifted.

Feet where they were. Change the knees' angle, hips a little back. Weight backward, yes, but so slightly the body did not drift. No retreat. No invitation for her to come and finish me.

From stepping in to cut, to cutting where I stood.

My daily practice swing. An armoured warrior's training: take the footwork away, prepare for fighting in the sky.

On the ground, ordinarily, useless. Footing available and you refuse to step? Pair hain, toh istemaal karo. You had legs for a reason.

Ordinarily.

Here she was, so deep inside my guard that this particular foolishness had changed sides.

Without the step, my cutting distance shortened.
One way to live among ten thousand ways to die.

At this distance, with her this close, the sword's striking section could still reach. Precisely because I had given up the step.

So simple once I thought of it. 'A cut requires a step' had meanwhile been sitting in my head like a very senior relation. Whole room occupied. Other suggestions could kindly remain outside.

Nearly got me killed, that respectable advice.

en.text:
Like hanging over a cliff by one finger.
That was exactly how I felt.

No time to release even a sigh of relief, though.

I had escaped that immediate death.
Now the situation had reached its final limit.

She saw my adjustment and did not hesitate. The same exquisitely slow advance continued.

For me, the distance now allowed only a direct cut. Still I could not rush into it.

Her shorter limbs left her some room. Even here she could use the Dropping Cut, or another counter. I still had to wait.

She, meanwhile, was in something like my earlier position. I could not counter; I could only strike back at the same time. Best for her to start first and reach me even a hair sooner.

But she did not attack.
Only came closer, little by little, watching my breath.

Why?
I did not know for certain.

Perhaps her pride again. A narrow victory was not enough? She wanted to frighten me into attacking, then defeat me completely with a counter?

Her killing intent grew heavier every moment. My fear grew with it. Loosen my hold on myself even a little and I might start shouting and hacking at her blindly.

Every bit of will I had went into holding that impulse down.

—A little more. Endure a little more.

The final turning point was close.

The distance would shrink
until she too could do nothing but cut.

No room for either side to work a counter.
Only the stroke itself. Only sword speed.

No scheme, no special art, no clever technique.
Even conditions. An equal contest, without question.

Who was faster?
Who was stronger?

One exchange would decide.

The last turning point.
The last opportunity.

...Close now.
I could have reached out and touched her.

Her face—◆
like the surface of a lake.

A bandit. Ex-Rokuhara. Nothing admirable in her history, nothing likable about the woman.

But at this moment, a warrior only. Nothing mixed into it.

A single-minded force, intent on defeating me, Kageaki Minato.

　――安堵して、吐息をこぼす暇など無かったが。

　そして、状況はここに窮まった。

　首領はこちらの変形を認めながら、去就に迷いもし

　この現況。
　こちらにとっては、もはや斬るのみの間だ。しかし、
まだ迂闊には仕掛けられない。

　俺に比せば四肢の短い敵手の側は、いくらか間合の
余裕を残している。
　これほどの近間でも切落、あるいはそれ以外の応じ

であれば今すぐにも先手を取り、髪一筋分でも早く剣
を相手へ届かせるが最上手だ。

　しかし――来ない。
　間合をじわりと削りながら、俺の呼吸を測るばかり
である。

　なぜか。
　確たるところは、定かではない。

　しかし、あるいは……これも己への自負心ゆえか。
　紙一重の勝利よりも、俺を威迫し誘い出しての迎撃
による完勝をこそ望むのか。

　確かに刻一刻と厚みを増す殺気は俺の恐怖心を煽り
立てる。
　精神の手綱をほんの少しでも緩めればその瞬間にも、
喚き立てながら無闇に斬り掛かってしまいそうな程に。

　衝動を堪えるには意志力の総動員を必要とした。
　
　――あとわずか。あとわずか、耐えねばならない。

　最後の節目が間もなく訪れる。

　間合はこのまま狭まり……
　遂に敵手も、ただ斬るばかりの距離に達する。

　互いに応じ技を凝こらす余地、最早なく。
　ただただ斬り合い、剣速を競うのみの間合に。

　策も術も技も無し。
　条件は五分と五分。疑いようもなく互角の勝負。

　どちらが、速いか。
　どちらが、強いか。

　一刀の振り合いにて、それを決する。

　最後の節目。
　最後の戦機だ。

　……間合は近接。
　手を伸ばせば届くほどの距離に、我が敵はいた。

　その貌は、◆
　――湖面の如く。

　彼女は山賊だ。
　六波羅上がりの、尊敬できぬ経歴を持つ、どう見た
ところでいけ好かない女だ。

　しかし今この瞬間は、純一の武人であって――ただ
それきりの存在だった。

　湊斗景明おれという敵に打ち克つ、
　ひたむきなちから。
